blocks.text: Organic nitrogen compounds are essential to life and to the modern world. Amino acids and nucleotides, the basis of proteins and nucleic acids, contain nitrogen. Amines and nitro compounds are important in the dye industry and in medicines; nylon, Kevlar and polyurethane are nitrogen-containing polymers; and nitrogen compounds are also found in food, fertilisers and explosives.

blocks.title: Interesting information: caffeine and theobromine
blocks.text: Caffeine in coffee and theobromine in chocolate are both organic nitrogen compounds; they are active compounds that make our mood happy. What is the difference between these two?

Amines are organic derivatives of ammonia in which one, two or three hydrogen atoms of NH3 are replaced by alkyl or aryl groups. The number of hydrogen atoms replaced is the basis of their classification. In IUPAC nomenclature amines are called alkanamines.

items: Primary amines: one alkyl or aryl group on the -NH2 group, e.g. methanamine CH3NH2, ethanamine CH3CH2NH2, propan-1-amine CH3CH2CH2NH2 and phenylamine (aniline) C6H5NH2.
Secondary amines: two groups on an -NH- group, e.g. N-methylmethanamine CH3NHCH3, N-methylethanamine CH3NHCH2CH3 and diphenylamine (C6H5)2NH.
Tertiary amines: three groups on the same nitrogen atom, e.g. N,N-dimethylmethanamine (CH3)3N and triphenylamine (C6H5)3N.
Quaternary ammonium salts: tetra-substituted nitrogen, e.g. tetramethylammonium chloride [(CH3)4N]+ Cl-.

blocks.alt: Four rows. Primary (one group on N): CH3NH2 methanamine, CH3CH2NH2 ethanamine, CH3CH2CH2NH2 propan-1-amine, C6H5NH2 phenylamine. Secondary (two groups): CH3NHCH3, CH3NHCH2CH3, (C6H5)2NH. Tertiary (three groups): (CH3)3N, (C6H5)3N. Quaternary salt: [(CH3)4N]+ Cl-, tetramethylammonium chloride.
blocks.caption: Classes of amines (original chart after the book's examples).
blocks.long_description: The class of an amine is set by how many carbon groups are attached to the nitrogen atom. This differs from alcohols and halogenoalkanes, where the class depends on the carbon that carries the functional group.

blocks.title: Branching at nitrogen
blocks.text: Whether an amine is primary, secondary or tertiary depends on the branching at the nitrogen atom, not at the carbon attached to it. This is not the same as for alcohols or halogenoalkanes.
